---
title: Software
description: Blender tools and simulation engines used across the projects.

Blender provides the scene and visual workflow. The simulation engine supplies the physical model. Keep their versions and responsibilities explicit when reproducing an example.

## SionnaRT-Bridge

**Public project · current inspected release: 2.1.0.**

Prepare procedural scenes in Blender, run Sionna RT, and inspect paths and spatial maps. Timeline sampling connects changing scene parameters with channel results; exports support subsequent analysis.

[Repository](https://github.com/fribas001/sionnart-bridge) · [Release 2.1.0](https://github.com/fribas001/sionnart-bridge/releases/tag/v2.1.0) · [Installation guide](https://github.com/fribas001/sionnart-bridge/blob/main/src/sionnart_bridge/README.md) · [Validation](https://github.com/fribas001/sionnart-bridge/blob/main/docs/validation.md)

The public release documents a tested Windows/CUDA environment. Its release checks do not establish support for every operating system or CPU configuration. Use the environment documented for the particular example; the extension and Sionna RT have independent version numbers.

## Mitsuba–Blender compatibility

**Public project.** A Blender 4.5 compatibility adaptation of Mitsuba–Blender, supporting scene export for the related workflows. Consult its own compatibility notes before combining it with a newer Blender installation.

[Repository](https://github.com/fribas001/mitsuba-blender-4.5-compatibility)

## DiffeRT-Bridge

**Local development · inspected source: 0.6.2.**

A companion Blender workflow using DiffeRT and JAX. The local comparison work examines how geometric tolerances, material values, numerical precision and export conventions affect agreement with Sionna.

[View the engine comparison](examples/engine-comparison.qmd). A public download for this local development version is not linked here.

## Mobility Bridge

**Local development · inspected source: 0.9.0.**

Connect JuPedSim pedestrian trajectories, SUMO traffic, and locally captured Skybrush drone motion to Blender displays and synchronized radio receivers. The inspected project also contains Antwerp UAV placement and evacuation studies.

[View the Antwerp case study](examples/antwerp.qmd). The illustration on that page comes from the earlier 0.6 moving-body demo; it is not evidence that every later feature was used in that scene.

## Choose the model for the question

| Question | Workflow |
|---|---|
| How do scene geometry and materials affect radio paths? | Blender + Sionna RT |
| How do two ray-tracing implementations compare under matched assumptions? | Sionna RT + DiffeRT comparison fixtures |
| How does receiver motion affect sampled radio links? | Mobility Bridge + the documented radio companion |
| How do I prepare and explain CT-derived geometry? | Blender modeling and the [conference talk](talks.qmd#ct-models) |

Absorbed power, internal tissue fields and SAR require a suitable electromagnetic model, material data and validation. They are not established by a propagation-path visualization alone. Keep those studies distinct from outdoor or indoor channel simulations.
